_readme: The NIST CCVS85 conformance ledger. Machine-readable, committed, and the single source of truth for where the work stands. Read it before doing anything; update it after every verified change. It replaces the hand-written HANDOFF-*.md files, which were re-derived from scratch each session and drifted. Protocol: .claude/skills/nist-grind/SKILL.md
goal: Every in-scope module at 100% on BOTH axes: every program compiles under `nist_conformance strict`, and every program runs to completion reporting 0 failures in its own CCVS report.

rules.never_ask_take_the_recommended_action: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29, given twice — do NOT stop to ask. When a choice arises, take the recommended course of action and proceed. Record the decision and the reasoning in this ledger so it can be reviewed after the fact, but never block the loop on a question.
rules.ix301m_out_of_scope: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29 — IX301M is OUT OF SCOPE. It tests INTERMEDIATE-subset flagging, and every construct it expects flagged (ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED, ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM, RECORD KEY IS, the NOT INVALID KEY phrases) is one PowerRustCOBOL implements. A high-subset implementation must not flag features it supports, so its 7 expectations are unreachable by design rather than by defect. IX is scored out of 41.
rules.start_rl_now: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29 — START RELATIVE I/O NOW, before IX is finished. This deliberately suspends GOLDEN RULE #9's one-module-at-a-time ordering: IX106A tests DELETE and REWRITE across relative, sequential and indexed files together, so IX cannot close without an RL engine. RL is the largest single piece of work outstanding.
rules.redb_becomes_the_default: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29 — fix duplicate-retrieval ordering in the redb engine, which already keeps a `seq` table for it, AND MAKE REDB THE DEFAULT disk engine. This avoids a PRCIDXD1 format change but is a large change in its own right: every `STORAGE IS DISK` file moves to redb, including the ones NC's and SQ's tests run through. Expect to spend iterations on the gate; revert rather than chase.
rules.everything_is_technical_debt: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29 — until all NIST implementation is done, there are NO new features; everything is technical debt being paid. Consequences: all of it goes on the `fixes` branch, none of it splits into a features commit, and none of it belongs on forum f=96. This overrides the usual feature/fix classification for the duration, and it covers RL (Relative I/O) too, which is missing COBOL-85 that should already have worked rather than a capability beyond the standard.
rules.no_forum_posts: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29 — do not post to cobolforo.es at all while the grind is running. Announcements are batched and are the operator's call.
rules.commit_and_push_before_stopping: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-29 — never end a session with work uncommitted. Commit and push `fixes` before stopping, subject only to the São Paulo push window (inside it, commit and defer the push).
rules.one_module_at_a_time: GOLDEN RULE #9 — finish the current module on both axes before starting the next. Record a tempting fix in another module under `parked` and move on.
rules.two_axes_never_conflated: Compile is the strictly weaker claim. Never quote it as if it meant the programs work.
rules.full_regression_after_every_change: Re-run the whole-suite strict census AND the execution pass for every finished module, not just the one in flight. The runtime is shared.
rules.deleted_is_not_passed: `***** ****TEST DELETED****` means the program failed its own setup and skipped the case. Track the DELETED count: it fell 108 -> 1 at 1.62.53 while the clean-program count barely moved, and that was real progress a failures-only reading would have missed.
rules.gate_protects_finished_modules_absolutel: The regression gate is ABSOLUTE for finished modules (NC, SQ) and for the whole-suite compile census: those figures must match exactly or the change is reverted. For the module IN FLIGHT the score may legitimately FALL when a harness-fidelity change makes the measurement more honest — assertions that were unreachable start running and start failing. That happened at 1.62.57: IX went 484 -> 482 PASS because IX103A finally found the file IX102A writes, so its scan ran 35 records deep instead of dying on the first READ, and two assertions that had never executed began to fail truthfully. When this happens, SAY SO explicitly with the reason; never revert a fidelity gain to protect a number, and never let a fidelity loss hide behind one.

_current_module_note: IF finished at 1.62.81. Next in `module_order` is IC (Inter-program communication), baselined at 1.62.81: 6 of 47 clean, 134 PASS / 129 FAIL — by far the weakest module measured so far, and the first whose subject is a whole language area (CALL / nested programs / LINKAGE) rather than a set of functions. Two members also fail to compile.

out_of_scope.why: CM is Communication, RW is Report Writer, OB* are the obsolete-element tests, EXEC85 is the suite driver.
out_of_scope.sg_ruling: 2026-08-29, operator: SG (Segmentation) is excluded too. Segmentation exists to fit a program into a machine too small to hold it — SECTION headers carry a segment-number and the runtime overlays the independent segments over one another. RustCOBOL is a 64-bit solution on 64-bit systems with more address space than any COBOL program can exhaust, so a segment-number COMPILES and has no effect at all. There is no behaviour for the module to measure, and scoring it would score a mechanism that will never exist. Its 13 programs still compile; they are reported N-A rather than deleted, so the exclusion stays visible.
out_of_scope.effect: 38 programs excluded from every score. The in-scope suite is 421, not 434.

IX.name: Indexed I/O
IX.finished_at: 1.62.76 — the RELATIVE engine closed IX106A's last four failures, which were the relative file it exercises alongside the sequential and indexed ones. Scored out of 41: IX301M is excluded from execution by operator ruling (see rules.ix301m_out_of_scope) and still counts in the compile census.

IF.name: Conditional
IF.finished_at: 1.62.81 — from a 24/45 baseline. Five causes, none of them in the module's own subject matter: a lexer separator rule (twice), a flagging gap, NUMVAL's argument grammar, an argument-list comparison, and a division overflow path. The Conditional module is a test of intrinsic functions, and every defect it found lived somewhere else.
IF.baselined_at: 1.62.77 — measured for the first time. 87.4% of 803 assertions. Two members CRASH the interpreter outright (IF124A, IF133A, exit 101) rather than failing, and a crash is a runtime panic, not a wrong answer — look at those first, they are the only two of their kind in the module. Three flagging members are heavily red (IF401M 14 FAIL / 0 PASS, IF402M 10/7, IF403M 8/5); IF401M asking for HIGH-subset flagging is the same shape as IX401M, which scores 10/10, so it is a real gap rather than a scoping question. The rest is a long tail of 1-12 failures across 18 members.

IC.name: Inter-program communication
IC.baselined_at: 1.62.81 — 6 of 47, 134 PASS / 129 FAIL. Corrected at 1.62.82 once the harness supplied each caller's callees: 10 of 25, 187 PASS / 71 FAIL, 72.5%.
IC.denominator_note: The execution denominator is 25, not 47. Twenty-two of IC's members are `SUBRTN` callees — separately compiled subprograms with no CCVS report of their own — so running one alone could only ever fail. They are still counted on the COMPILE axis, where the module remains 45 of 47. When comparing against the 1.62.81 baseline use 6 -> 10 of 25.
IC.shape: Unlike NC/SQ/IX/RL/IF this module's subject is a whole language area — CALL, nested programs, LINKAGE, INITIAL, EXTERNAL — so expect fewer, larger causes rather than a long tail. No crashes and no timeouts: the programs run and get the answers wrong. Two members do not compile (IC224A: `unexpected token in statement: EndCall`).

SG.name: Segmentation
SG.why: Operator ruling, 2026-08-29 — see out_of_scope.sg_ruling. Its 13 programs still compile; there is simply no segmentation behaviour on a 64-bit runtime for them to exercise.

RL.name: Relative I/O
RL.finished_at: 1.62.77 — from a 14/35 baseline in one session. Scored out of 34: RL301M is excluded from execution by the same ruling as IX301M (rules.ix301m_out_of_scope) and still counts in the compile census, where it passes.
RL.engine_landed: 1.62.76 — `cobolt-runtime/src/relative.rs`, container PRCREL1, plus MEMORY. All seven verbs dispatch on FileOrganization::Relative. The same version taught the harness RL's ten chained members, which is what ended the four timeouts.
RL.what_actually_closed_it: The engine was the smaller half. Three front-end fixes at 1.62.77 took RL from 24 to 34: (1) `RELATIVE data-name` with the word KEY omitted was read as a bare organization clause and the key silently dropped, so every random WRITE returned 24 — eight programs, one clause; (2) file status 14, a sequential READ whose record number needs more digits than the RELATIVE KEY item holds — the PICTURE's width is part of the file's behaviour; (3) an unterminated conditional phrase (`WRITE ... INVALID KEY GO TO X` with no END-WRITE) read past the enclosing ELSE, so RL210A did not parse at all. The last one is general, not relative-specific, and raised the whole-suite compile census to 423.
RL.operator_ruling: 2026-08-29 — IMPLEMENT Relative file support as the NIST suite expects it, and treat it as TECHNICAL DEBT, not a feature: RELATIVE is COBOL-85 that should already have worked, so under GOLDEN RULE #4 it is a fix. It goes on the `fixes` branch like everything else, needs no features commit, and is not an f=96 item. This is the one place in the queue where building missing capability is authorised; elsewhere a genuine grammar gap is still recorded and parked, not invented.
RL.starting_point: HISTORICAL, superseded by engine_landed above. Before 1.62.76 there was no RELATIVE engine at all: the parser accepted `ORGANIZATION IS RELATIVE` (FileOrganization::Relative) and nothing in the runtime ever matched that variant — no dispatch, no engine, no diagnostic — so a program declaring it compiled cleanly and then misbehaved silently.
scope_notes: A RELATIVE file is addressed by RELATIVE KEY, an integer record number from 1, not by a key embedded in the record.
SELECT carries `RELATIVE KEY IS data-name`; the parser must keep it as RECORD KEY is kept for INDEXED.
All three access modes: SEQUENTIAL (records in relative-number order), RANDOM (by RELATIVE KEY), DYNAMIC (both).
Verbs to dispatch on FileOrganization::Relative: OPEN, CLOSE, READ (random and NEXT/PREVIOUS), WRITE, REWRITE, DELETE, START.
File statuses the module tests: 00, 02, 10, 21, 22, 23, 24 (boundary violation on WRITE past the end), 43, 46, 47, 48, 49.
A deleted slot must stay addressable and read as not-present — a relative file is a numbered slot table, not a dense list.
Reuse the storage split the INDEXED engines already have (STORAGE IS MEMORY | DISK) rather than inventing a fourth container format.
RL.sequencing: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-29 — the operator ruled START RL NOW, before IX is finished (see rules.start_rl_now). IX106A cannot pass without it. It is large enough to be worth planning before coding, but as technical debt it does NOT need the feature pipeline — plan it in the ledger's work_queue and implement on `fixes`.

work_queue.title: A READ that errors inside a GO TO loop spins forever
work_queue.worth: Robustness, not score. Latent since 1.62.69 and found by accident; no suite member hits it today, but the only thing that would catch it is the harness timeout.
work_queue.evidence: Written while trying to dump IX215A's data. The reader declared a schema the file does not have, so OPEN returned 39 and every following READ returned 47. The loop is the ordinary CCVS shape — `L. READ F AT END GO TO E END-READ ... GO TO L.` — and it never terminated; the command was killed after five minutes.
work_queue.cause: 1.62.69 made the AT END phrase fire only for status 10, which is correct: 47 is not the AT END condition. But with no USE declarative the statement now falls through and the loop repeats the same failing READ. Before that change the phrase fired on any non-zero status and the loop exited, which was wrong for the right reason.
work_queue.the_question: COBOL-85 says an unhandled I-O error invokes the file's USE declarative, and with none declared the result is implementor-defined. Spinning is a poor choice. Terminating the run with a diagnostic, the way an unhandled runtime error already does, is defensible and would surface the real problem instead of a timeout. This is a design decision, so it is recorded rather than taken.
work_queue.caveat: Do NOT fix it by making AT END fire on other statuses again — that reintroduces the defect 1.62.69 corrected, and IX114A depends on the current behaviour.

work_queue.resolved_at: 1.62.78 — and the `next_probe` advice was worth its line: the panic message named interpreter.rs:10771 (`args[1]` of FUNCTION MOD), which was the whole diagnosis. The cause was in the LEXER, two crates away: a separator comma followed by a sign was dropped, so `FUNCTION MOD(A, -3)` became `A -3` and read as one subtraction. Fixing it took IF from 24 to 32 clean — the two crashes were the visible edge of a defect that was also costing assertions in six other members.
work_queue.title: RESOLVED — IF124A and IF133A crash the interpreter (exit 101)
work_queue.worth: Two programs, and the only two of their kind in the module — a crash is a runtime panic, not a wrong answer, so it is a different class of defect from the other 101 failures and almost certainly a smaller fix.
work_queue.evidence: Measured at 1.62.77 baselining IF. Both report `crashed: exit exit status: 101`, which is a Rust panic rather than a COBOL-level failure. No assertions are scored for either, so their true contribution to the module is unknown until they run.
work_queue.next_probe: Extract each and run it by hand — the panic message names the file and line, which is usually the whole diagnosis. `extract IF124A > IF124A.cbl` then run it with the two switches; do not read the CCVS report first, read stderr.

work_queue.resolved_at: 1.62.79 — 44 of 44 matched, 0 wrong. It WAS a real gap, not the IX301M scoping question: `flag_high_subset` flags constructs above the COBOL-85 high subset regardless of whether we implement them, and intrinsic functions arrived with the 1989 addendum. One rule covered all three members. Note the trap for next time: my first reading said `0 expected messages` because these members write the marker in UPPERCASE and the grep was case-sensitive.
work_queue.title: RESOLVED — IF401M / IF402M / IF403M ask for subset flagging we do not emit
work_queue.worth: 32 of the module's 101 failures sit in three programs.
work_queue.the_question: IF401M is the *high*-subset shape, the same as IX401M which scores 10 of 10 — so this is a real gap in `flagging::flag_high_subset`, not the intermediate-subset scoping question that ruled IX301M and RL301M out. Check each member's own header before assuming which kind it is: a member asking a high-subset implementation to flag features it does NOT support is in scope, one asking it to flag features it DOES support is not.
work_queue.next_probe: Read the `Message expected` comments in each and compare against what `flag_high_subset` emits today.

work_queue.resolved_at: 1.62.84 — a BY REFERENCE parameter is now an ALIAS onto its argument (`env.set_alias`, the same redirection `SET ADDRESS OF` uses), released when the call returns. IC 187 -> 194 PASS, 71 -> 62 FAIL. Only the parameter is aliased: a group parameter's subordinate items keep resolving by name to the caller's, which is what the dead end below got wrong.
work_queue.title: RESOLVED — A called program's data is the caller's, whenever the two use the same data-name
work_queue.worth: The largest IC bucket by far — roughly 30 of the 71 failures across IC101A, IC103A, IC201A and IC225A, all of them some form of 'value changed by call' or 'value not returned'.
work_queue.diagnosis: DECISIVE, from IC201A CALL-TEST-02. It calls `IC202A USING DN1, DN2, DN1, DN4` — the third argument is DN1, not DN3 — and IC202A writes through its third LINKAGE item, which it happens to call `DN3`. The caller's own unrelated `DN3` is overwritten, because `push_local_scope` skips a name the caller already has, so the two are the SAME slot. The test checks exactly that: `DN3 VALUE CHANGED BY CALL`.
work_queue.where: `CobolEnvironment::push_local_scope` (environment.rs) and the nested-program CALL arm of `exec_call` (interpreter.rs, ~line 8120). Binding today is by-name copy-in / copy-out: the parameter NAMES are set from the arguments before the call and written back after.
work_queue.next_probe: Alias, do not copy — and read the `shadowing-a-callees-names-without-aliasing-them` dead end first, which is the attempt that got this wrong. Bind the callee's parameter and everything subordinate to it to the caller's storage for the length of the call (`addr_aliases` already redirects `resolve_name` for pointers). The subordinate-item case is what broke the naive fix: a group parameter's children must resolve through the alias to the caller's children, not to fresh slots.
work_queue.caveat: BY CONTENT must NOT alias — it is a copy taken at entry with no write-back — and IC201A's CALL-TEST-03 tests that alongside ON OVERFLOW.

work_queue.resolved_at: 1.62.82 — and it was a harness gap, exactly as `the_question` suspected. The suite declares each callee on its own control card, `*HEADER,COBOL,IC101A,SUBRTN,IC102A`, and the splitter only knew `SUBPRG`, so every callee took its CALLER's name and `extract IC102A` produced nothing. Callers now run with their callees concatenated into one run unit: IC 6 -> 10 of its 25 tests, 134 -> 187 PASS. **The trap:** SUBPRG and SUBRTN are NOT synonyms — SUBPRG names the next test of the same group (IX101A,SUBPRG,IX102A is the producer chain) and every one is a scored member. Treating them alike excluded SQ203A and took SQ from 85/85 to 84/84.
work_queue.title: RESOLVED — IC's callers need their subprograms, which are separate suite members
work_queue.worth: Very likely most of the module's 129 failures, and it is a MEASUREMENT question before it is a runtime one — read this before writing any code.
work_queue.evidence: Measured at 1.62.81. IC108A's report says `SUBPROGRAM IC109A ERROR`, `SUBPROGRAM IC110A ERROR`, `SUBPROGRAM IC111A ERROR` and `IC109A CALLED N TIMES` — IC109A, IC110A and IC111A are separate members of the suite. IC101A fails all five of its `CALL...USING DATA-NM` tests the same way. The harness runs one source file through `rcrun`, so a `CALL "IC109A"` has nothing to call.
work_queue.the_question: This is the IX/RL chained-member problem in a different shape: there the producer wrote a FILE the consumer read, here the callee IS the program the caller invokes. The fix is likely in the harness (concatenate or otherwise make the called members available to the caller), not in the runtime — and confirming that FIRST avoids inventing a CALL defect that does not exist. See the ledger's `harness-limits-look-like-runtime-regressions` lesson.
work_queue.next_probe: Extract IC108A and IC109A, run IC108A by hand, and read what `CALL "IC109A"` actually does — a failed CALL, a no-op, or an ON EXCEPTION path. Then check how the suite expects separately-compiled programs to be presented: CCVS85 members carry their own IDENTIFICATION DIVISION, so several may be intended to compile into one run unit.
work_queue.caveat: Do NOT assume every IC failure is this. IC106A's are about INDEX and REDEFINES items in the LINKAGE SECTION, which is a real runtime question and independent of how the subprogram is supplied.

work_queue.resolved_at: 1.62.80 — 18 of the 19 closed, in three causes. The `next_probe` guess was half right: MAX/MIN/ORD-MAX/ORD-MIN WERE one family and one cause (the as_f64() comparison, plus first-of-a-tie for the ordinal pair), but ACOS/ASIN/ATAN were NOT a precision question at all — they were a division defect, `1 / SQRT3` coming out as 1 because the overflow fallback used the dividend's scale. RANGE turned out to be a third thing entirely; see if-range-05-glued-sign.
work_queue.title: RESOLVED — IF's last 19 failures are all numeric-intrinsic results
work_queue.evidence: Measured at 1.62.79. ATAN 4 (IF104A), MAX 3 (IF119A), MIN 3 (IF123A), ORD-MAX 4 (IF128A), ASIN 2 (IF103A), ACOS 1 (IF101A), ORD-MIN 1 (IF129A), RANGE 1 (IF132A). Every one is a value comparison, not a status or a parse — the functions all run.

work_queue.resolved_at: 1.62.81 — done, and it cost nothing. The `why_not_done_yet` risk assessment below was too pessimistic in one specific way: it assumed the rule had to apply after any operand. Restricting the guard to a NUMERIC LITERAL or `)` before the sign removed the whole PICTURE / BY -1 exposure, because those follow a word. All five finished modules and the compile census were exact on the first run.
work_queue.title: RESOLVED — IF132A F-RANGE-05: a sign glued to a literal is a sign, not an operator
work_queue.worth: The LAST failing assertion in IF. Nothing else stands between the module and 45/45.
work_queue.evidence: `COMPUTE WS-NUM = FUNCTION RANGE(10.2 -0.2, 5.6, -15.6).` — there is NO comma between the first two arguments. The test expects 25.8, which is 10.2 - (-15.6), so the suite means four arguments. We read `10.2 - 0.2` as one subtraction and get three, giving 25.6.
work_queue.the_rule: COBOL-85 tells a sign from a binary operator by the space AFTER it: a binary operator must be surrounded by spaces, so `10.2 -0.2` is two operands and `10.2 - 0.2` is one subtraction. This is the same rule that motivated the comma exception at 1.62.78, but the other half of it — there the comma made the boundary explicit, here nothing does.
work_queue.why_not_done_yet: It is the riskiest change left. Implementing it means the LEXER treats a glued `+`/`-` after an operand as a sign, which touches every arithmetic expression in every module rather than one function's arguments. A program that writes `A -3` meaning subtraction changes behaviour silently — such a program is already non-conforming, but silence is the problem. Benefit: 1 assertion.
work_queue.next_probe: If attempted: guard it on the PREVIOUS token being one that can end an operand (identifier, literal, `)`), so PICTURE templates and `BY -1` are untouched; then run all five finished modules plus the compile census before believing it. The semicolon episode (see dead_ends) is the model — a lexer change has no module boundary.

work_queue.resolved_at: 1.62.77 — all of it. The bucketing advice below was right: the five programs sharing the 'CREATE RL-FD2' message shared one cause (the `RELATIVE data-name` clause), and it closed eight programs at once. RL117A's lone failure was file status 14; RL301M was ruled out of scope.
work_queue.title: RESOLVED — RL's 11 programs that still fail, after the engine landed
work_queue.worth: 38 failing assertions and 11 of 35 programs. This is the whole of what is left in the module.
work_queue.evidence: Measured at 1.62.76, from `fails RL`. RL109A 7, RL112A 6, RL204A 6, RL301M 5, RL113A 3, RL114A 3, RL117A 3, RL110A 2, RL116A 2, RL118A 1. Buckets that recur across several members: (a) 'CREATE RL-FD2 ... INCORRECT COUNT' / 'STATUS/WRITE' in RL112A/113A/114A/117A/204A, which is one shared cause across five programs and so the first thing to look at; (b) 'DUPLICATE KEY SHOULD HAVE OCCURRED' in RL118A and 'INVALID WRITE' in RL116A, both about the status a WRITE onto an occupied slot returns; (c) RL301M, which is a flagging member and may be the same intermediate-subset scoping question as IX301M.
work_queue.next_probe: Re-run `fails RL` and bucket by message before touching anything — five programs sharing one message is a root cause, not five bugs. Start with the CREATE RL-FD2 bucket.

work_queue.resolved_at: 1.62.73 + 1.62.74 — redb became the default disk engine (which keeps the `seq` table this needs) and its REWRITE now reassigns the sequence when an alternate value changes. The PRCIDXD1 format change was never needed. Kept for the diagnosis, not as work.
work_queue.title: RESOLVED — A REWRITE that CHANGES an alternate key must join the end of its new duplicate set
work_queue.worth: IX215A's last 2 failures, and very likely IX211A's 2 as well — its symptoms are small ordering errors in a walk over duplicate keys.
work_queue.diagnosis: DECISIVE, from the data rather than a repro. IX215A GF-08 reads record 176 and rewrites it with ALTKEY2 = 'DCDCDCDCDC100ALTKEY2'. GF-09 then reads record **4** and rewrites it with the SAME value, deliberately creating a duplicate set of two, and STARTs on the 2-character generic key 'DC' expecting record **176** — the entry created FIRST. A dump of the file confirms exactly two records carry that value, 4 and 176. We return 4.
work_queue.the_rule: Duplicates are retrieved in the order their entries entered the set. Record 176 joined in GF-08, record 4 in GF-09, so 176 comes first. We order by the record's ORIGINAL insertion sequence — record 4 was written before 176 when the file was built — which is a position record 4 never held in this set. CLAUDE.md's note that 'the record keeps its original insertion sequence across a REWRITE' is right only while the alternate VALUE is unchanged; when the value changes the record leaves one duplicate set and joins another, at the end.
work_queue.where: Disk engine (the default): `alt_tree_key(ks, rec, recid)` appends the RecordId, so ordering within one alternate value is by RecordId — permanently the original write order. Fixing it means the tiebreaker must be a per-entry sequence assigned when the entry is inserted, not the RecordId. That is a container-format consideration for PRCIDXD1, so size it before starting. The redb engine already keeps a `seq` table for this and may only need its sequence reassigned on a value-changing REWRITE; the in-memory engine uses a BTreeSet of primary keys and has the same original-order problem.
work_queue.caveat: Only a REWRITE that CHANGES the alternate value reassigns the sequence. One that leaves it alone must keep its position, which is what the existing behaviour and the disk-parity note are about.
work_queue.sizing_2026_08_29: Measured, not estimated. The disk engine builds an alternate entry key as `altvalue || recid.to_be_bytes()` (alt_tree_key, ~line 820) and `index_remove` rebuilds that same key from the OLD record plus the recid — which works only because the suffix is derivable from the record. A sequence suffix is not derivable, so removal and value-changing rewrite would need a persisted per-alternate `recid -> seq` map. The container header carries a version field (currently 1u16 at offset 8), so a bump is possible, but this is a PRCIDXD1 FORMAT CHANGE to the DEFAULT on-disk engine — the same engine NC's and SQ's file tests run through. Cost: format version 2, a new persisted structure, changes to index_insert / index_remove / rewrite, the key_prefix klen logic, and a read path for version-1 files. Benefit: 4 assertions in 2 programs (IX215A, IX211A).
alternatives: Do the format change. Correct, and the only route to 42/42 on this axis, but the most expensive remaining item and the one with real risk to the protected modules.
Do it in the redb engine only, which already keeps a `seq` table for exactly this — cheap there, but redb is not the default, so the suite would not see it without switching the default.
Accept it as a known deviation and record it. Duplicate retrieval order after a value-changing REWRITE is a narrow corner; the cost/benefit is poor at 4 assertions.
work_queue.operator_call: This one is a judgement call about cost, not a diagnosis gap. Do not start the format change without a decision.

work_queue.resolved_at: 1.62.74 — IX215A runs clean. Kept because its `ruled_out` list is the record of four repros that all passed while the real defect was elsewhere; that is the entry's lasting value.
work_queue.title: RESOLVED — see rewrite-into-a-duplicate-set-keeps-a-position-it-never-had
work_queue.worth: 2 failures, the last two in IX215A.
work_queue.evidence: Record 176 is rewritten so its ALTKEY2 becomes 'DCDCDCDCDC100ALTKEY2'. The test then does `START IX-FD1 KEY IS EQUAL TO R-ALTKEY2-1-2` — positions 1-2 of ALTKEY2, so the generic key is just 'DC' — and reads NEXT, expecting record 176. It computes 4. The qualified-name variant of the same test expects 190 and computes 12. Both return a small record number where a large one is expected, so the search lands on the wrong member of the duplicate set rather than failing outright.
ruled_out: NOT the construct in isolation. dead_ends.what: Make `push_local_scope` SHADOW a name the caller already has instead of skipping it, so a called program's data is its own.
dead_ends.why_it_failed: IC 10 -> 5 of 25, 187 -> 138 PASS, and one member began timing out. Binding is by-name copy-in/copy-out: only the names in `PROCEDURE DIVISION USING` are copied in. Shadowing gives the callee fresh slots for EVERY name it declares — including the subordinate items of a group parameter — and those are not copied in, so a callee that reads `GRP-01`'s children saw their initial values instead of the caller's data. The old aliasing-by-collision was accidentally right for exactly that case.
dead_ends.the_defect_is_still_real: IC201A CALL-TEST-02 does `CALL "IC202A" USING DN1, DN2, DN1, DN4` — the third argument is DN1, not DN3. IC202A writes through its third LINKAGE item, which it happens to call `DN3`, and the caller's own unrelated `DN3` is overwritten because the two are the same slot. The test checks precisely that: `DN3 VALUE CHANGED BY CALL`.
dead_ends.what_to_do_instead: Alias, do not copy. Bind the callee's parameter name — and everything subordinate to it — to the CALLER's storage for the length of the call, the way `addr_aliases` already redirects `resolve_name` for pointers. Then a group parameter's children resolve through the alias to the caller's children, a name the callee declares that is NOT a parameter gets a private slot, and BY CONTENT is a copy made once at entry with no write-back. Size the subordinate-item part first: that is where this attempt broke.

dead_ends.what: Keep a separator COMMA OR SEMICOLON when the next token is a sign, so `FUNCTION MOD(A, -3)` stops reading as one subtraction.
dead_ends.why_it_failed: It fixed IF but broke NC245A, which had been passing — NC 95/95 -> 94/95, a protected baseline. NC245A is the separator test itself and writes `MOVE ELEM3( +3; +5, +10) TO TEMP`: a semicolon is never a list separator in COBOL, only decoration, and no parser eats one, so keeping it is a parse error rather than a separator.
dead_ends.what_to_do_instead: The exception belongs to the COMMA alone. Both the function-argument and subscript parsers already eat a comma between elements, so keeping it there costs nothing; the semicolon has no such reader anywhere.
dead_ends.the_lesson: The regression was invisible in the module being worked on and only showed up in the whole-suite gate. Run every finished module after ANY lexer or parser change — those two crates have no module boundary.

dead_ends.what: Give every member of a module ONE shared work directory so the CCVS85 file chain works.
